newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee ends up on NY, Colombia news.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee ends up on NY, Colombia news.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures were knocked down from their peaks by late selling but prices still finished higher on earlier trade buying and spec short-covering as buy-stops were triggered.
Taking a cue from a run-up in New York, the market advanced to the highest level in a week before ending with pared gains on market-on-close selling.
New York arabicas were lifted by news of a truck drivers' strike in Colombia and concerns over a squeeze on New York's September contract.
"I guess the Colombian news came at the right time," said one trader. But unlike the crippling stoppages seen in recent months, traders said the situation this time around could be less explosive.
"It won't make a 10 cent-rally. It will be a swift rally," the same trader said.
LIFFE benchmark November contract finished the day $52 firmer at $1,535 per tonne after a peak at $1,570, the highest since August 12.
September, which enters first notice day on September 1, led actives with 2,481 lots as players rolled the positions far forward. It gained $59 on the day at $1,520.

Sept/Nov spread, which hovered at $18-$23 in the morning, ended the day at $15. Traders said it would be attractive to roll forward the September positions and hedge coffee against November given the November premium.
Overall volume was a modest 5,575 lots.
A strike by Colombian truck drivers in Colombia's main Pacific coast port of Buenaventura has blocked the export of about 21,000 60-kg bags of coffee, a truckers' leader said on Tuesday.

About 60 percent of Colombia's coffee exports are shipped out of Buenaventura. The strike began late Saturday but passed virtually unnoticed given that it came during a three-day bank holiday weekend.

"No trucks are going in or out of the port. We have about 3,000 trucks immobilized in and around Buenaventura and about 30 of them are loaded with about 700 bags each of coffee," Javier Suarez, head of the Colombian Truck Drivers' Association ACC told Reuters.
The London market took a tumble on Monday on speculative selling and long liquidation as the November contract breached the recent low at $1,472 before hitting the floor at $1,445.
